thread:
Rafael Mendes: on-call handoff for Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive pilot (this week)

Runbook is live + linked from on-call index:
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Dedicated+Autoscaler+Troubleshooting+Runbook

What to page on (during pilot):
1) `dedicated.queue_depth` sustained high (>= 10 min) AND p95 latency regression for a Dedicated deployment w/ predictive enabled.
2) `autoscaler.bound_hit{bound="max"}` firing AND queue_depth rising (means customer is hard-capped, likely needs comms / config change).
3) `autoscaler.min_unmet` (min bound not met) > 5 min (usually region capacity shortage or provisioning failure).
4) Predictor issues: forecast staleness > 15 min OR forecast provider errors > 5% for pilot accounts.

Dashboards:
- Dedicated Autoscaling: Bounds/Predictive Overview (Grafana)
  https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/dedicated-autoscaling-bounds
- Per-deployment drilldown (same folder) -> "Scale Events" + "Desired vs Bounded"

Known failure modes we’ve seen / expect:
- Predictor returns null/stale -> if any downscale happens, verify we’re not dropping below safe baseline (we have a guard now, but still watch).
- Oscillation when predictive is on + traffic is spiky/noisy. Cooldowns help, but if it’s causing customer-visible jitter, disable predictive for that deployment.
- Max bound saturation: customers set max too low vs ramp; autoscaler does the right thing (clamps) but queues build.
- Min bound unmet during region shortage: autoscaler will keep retrying but cannot conjure GPUs; we need to surface degraded state + comms.

Quick mitigations:
- If customer impact: toggle predictive OFF (reactive-only) for the deployment (bounds still enforced).
- If queue is climbing and max bound hit: confirm it’s expected (hard cap) then loop in CS to discuss raising max.
- If min unmet: escalate to infra (capacity) + SRE; do not keep flapping config.

Escalation:
- Autoscaler: @Vanessa Ortiz / @Keiko Yamamoto
- Control plane / policy eval issues: @Ethan Park
- Dashboards/alerts: @Allison Grant / @Sergio Costa
- Customer comms/escalations: @Dev Patel + @Lauren Bishop

Ping here if anything looks off. :rotating_light:

Miles Thornton: thx. for paging criteria, do we want to explicitly call out “max bound hit + rising queue” vs “max bound hit alone”? bound_hit alone might be noisy if customers run near cap.

Rafael Mendes: yep good call. page only when bound_hit correlates w/ customer pain signals (queue_depth up + latency). bound_hit alone = ticket/heads-up, not page.

PagerDuty Bot: Acknowledged: "Dedicated Autoscaling Pilot - Queue depth sustained" by Miles Thornton

Keiko Yamamoto: one more failure mode: predictive can “lead” too early and cause extra spend. not a page, but if you see sustained overprovisioning (desired >> actual demand) flag it in #eng-infra so we can tune dampening.

Allison Grant: dashboard has a panel "Prediction error (MAPE)" + "Over/undershoot". if you see MAPE > ~0.5 sustained for a pilot acct, drop a note; we’re collecting examples.

Vanessa Ortiz: re: disable predictive — safest path is via feature flag on the deployment, not editing bounds. bounds changes are rate-limited now, but still prefer not to churn config during incident.

Lauren Bishop: +1. if you disable predictive for a pilot account, please leave a comment in the pilot tracker + tag me. we want to follow up w/ the customer same day.

Dev Patel: for CS: if max bound saturation is the issue, pls grab screenshot of "Desired vs Bounded" + queue panel and attach to support ticket. helps us explain "it’s respecting your cap" vs "platform failed to scale".

Mina Haddad: routing note: if bounded state is active (max hit) and queueing grows, smart routing may start fallback to compatible variant if configured. don’t assume it’s a bug; check routing events panel.

Ethan Park: also, if Console shows validation errors on min/max edits (min>max, cooldown too low), that’s expected. if you see policy eval errors in logs (`capacity-policy-service` 5xx), page platform-oncall.

Miles Thornton: can we add a TL;DR command to dump effective policy + last decision? easier than digging in logs.

Keiko Yamamoto: internal CLI exists now:
`rdw admin scaling-policy dump --deployment <id> --region <region>`
outputs effective min/max, cooldown, predictive mode, last 10 decisions + reasons (requested vs bounded). it’s in the runbook under “debug tools”.

Rafael Mendes: awesome. i’ll update the on-call note in the runbook index too. also reminder: during pilot, if you’re unsure whether to page customer vs infra, page SRE + infra first; we’d rather be noisy than miss a min_unmet or runaway queue.

Sergio Costa: fwiw alert routing: “max bound saturation + queue buildup” goes to dedicated-oncall; “predictor stale/errors” goes to infra-oncall; “min unmet” goes to both. should reduce ping-pong.

Miles Thornton: got it. :thumbsup:
